title: Susceptibility of qudit-qudit entanglement to quantum noise: insights from the negativity rank
abstract: One aspect of complexity for quantum many-body systems resides in their ability to exhibit entanglement, uniquely quantum correlations central to quantum computation. To quantitatively explore the diminishing effect that quantum noise has on entanglement resources, we focus on the negativity witness, an entanglement measure based on local time reversal transformations that provides a perfect witness in simple physical contexts. Beyond calculation of the negativity, we analyze the associated eigenvalue spectra of partially transposed density matrices for qudit-qudit bipartitions, finding that higher negativity rank provides greater(reduced) robustness to targeted(depolarizing) noise. In particular, we extend the maximum number of separable states that can be arbitrarily mixed into an entangled pure ensemble while retaining negativity to be exactly equal to the original negativity rank. Furthermore, we report how understanding the role of the negativity rank with respect to the completely depolarizing channel allows direct calculation of (1) certain noise boundaries for the Absolutely Positive Partial Transpose (APPT) subspace beyond which no unitary operator is capable of generating negativity and (2) the maximum qutrit-qutrit APPT purity. Beyond proving tight bounds and contributing to the ongoing search for APPT entanglement, these results expand our understanding of the nuanced relationship between computation with entanglement and practical environments for operating quantum devices.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to measure how quantum noise degrades entanglement in qudit systems using the negativity rank. By analyzing the partially transposed density matrix, the authors establish that the negativity rank dictates the robustness of entanglement against noise. The results provide actionable bounds for quantum device design, particularly concerning the Absolutely Positive Partial Transpose (APPT) subspace.
main_problem: The paper aims to quantitatively explore how quantum noise diminishes entanglement resources in complex quantum many-body systems.
main_result: Higher negativity rank provides greater robustness to targeted noise, and the negativity rank allows for direct calculation of noise boundaries for the APPT subspace and the maximum qutrit-qutrit APPT purity.
method: The study utilizes the negativity witness, analyzing the eigenvalue spectra of partially transposed density matrices ($ho^\Gamma$) to quantify entanglement robustness.
model_or_system: The focus is on qudit-qudit entanglement, analyzing mixed ensembles under the influence of global depolarizing noise channels.
key_observables: Negativity, Negativity Rank ($n_-$), Absolutely Positive Partial Transpose (APPT) subspace, and Purity.
important_parameters: Depolarizing noise parameter ($p$), and the dimension of the qudits ($d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes $p$ is small enough such that the negativity rank remains constant under the depolarizing channel, and it discusses the computational difficulty of general entanglement detection.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates depolarized trajectories of entanglement classifications in the two-qudit Bloch sphere, showing Type 1 and Type 2 trajectories relative to the APPT boundary.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the problem using the negativity witness, analyzing the effect of noise on entanglement boundaries (APPT/ASEP), and deriving specific quantitative results for noise boundaries and maximum purity.
why_interesting: It provides concrete, quantitative tools (negativity rank) to predict the operational limits of quantum devices when subjected to realistic noise models, which is crucial for quantum information science.
